title: The Lonely Sock
statement:
After washing, all socks are in one pile. Every sock has a colour code (a positive integer). Each colour appears in exactly **two** socks, except one colour that appears only **once**: that is the lonely sock.

Find the colour code of the lonely sock.
input:
The first line contains an odd integer **n**, the number of socks.

The second line contains n integers a[1], ..., a[n], the colour codes. Exactly one value appears once; every other value appears exactly twice.
output: Print the colour code that appears only once.
hints: A hash map that counts every value works.
There is a trick with XOR: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x. What happens if you XOR all the numbers together?
editorial:
XOR all the numbers. Equal numbers cancel each other (x ^ x = 0), the order does not matter, and the only value left is the lonely one. This needs no extra memory. Counting with a hash map is also O(n) and perfectly fine.

Complexity: O(n) time, O(1) memory.
